explain.say: Plant one potato and you can dig up ten or more. A potato is not a root; it is a swollen underground stem that stores food, and it can grow a whole new plant.

explain.say: The eyes on a potato are buds. In warm, damp soil they sprout shoots, fed by the starch stored in the old potato, until the leaves reach the light.

faq.q: What are the eyes on a potato?
faq.a: The eyes are buds, like the buds on a twig. Each can sprout a shoot, which is why one potato cut into pieces, each with an eye, can grow several plants.

faq.q: Why is a potato full of starch?
faq.a: Starch is how the plant stores the sugar its leaves make. The stored food lets a new plant sprout next year before it has any leaves of its own.
asks: What is stored in a potato?

faq.a: No. A potato is a tuber, a swollen underground stem. You can tell because it has buds, the eyes, which roots never have, and it turns green in the light.
In light, potatoes make chlorophyll, and alongside it a bitter natural poison called solanine. That is why potatoes are stored in the dark and green parts should be cut away.
asks: Are green potatoes safe to eat?

faq.q: Do potato plants have flowers and seeds?
faq.a: Yes. They grow white, pink or purple flowers and small green berries with seeds, but the berries are poisonous. Farmers plant seed potatoes because they grow exactly like the parent.

facts: A potato is a stem tuber, and its eyes are buds.
Potatoes grown from tubers are clones of the parent plant.
Green parts of potatoes can contain solanine, a natural toxin.
